page: Amazon Web Services c8g.2xlarge is an ARM64 compute-optimized server powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 8 dedicated physical cores with single-threaded execution per core. It features 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core allocation. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography enabled. No local storage or GPU hardware is included.

Benchmark data shows strong performance in memory bandwidth for large-block read-only operations, reaching 188.91 GB/sec, which places it in the top 25% of tested servers. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is also strong at 14.22 GB/sec. However, the instance exhibits a performance bottleneck in cryptographic operations, with the PassMark CPU encryption test scoring 1509.87, placing it in the bottom 25%. Large-model LLM inference is also a weak point, with prompt processing for a medium 7B model scoring in the bottom 10% at 15.58 tokens/sec. Most other compute, web serving, and database benchmarks fall within the average middle 50% range.

The c8g.2xlarge offers a compute-focused hardware profile with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, making it resource-dense for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. Because it utilizes custom ARM64 architecture, it provides qualitative cost-efficiency advantages for workloads optimized for ARM, though it lacks x86-specific instruction sets like AVX or AMX. The instance is suited for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose compute tasks, while being less optimal for heavy cryptographic processing or large language model inference.
